coreProposition: OAuth refresh should be modeled as a split-commit workflow whenever remote credential issuance and local durable persistence are separate operations; persistence failure after remote success is a distinct partial-success state that must remain visible for reconciliation.

openingMove.purpose: Start at the moment the authorization server has already issued fresh credentials but local durable storage reports failure.

argumentNodes.question: Why is persistence failure not ordinary refresh failure?
argumentNodes.claim: Remote issuance has succeeded while local durability has not, so the two authorities have advanced differently.
argumentNodes.readerProgress: The reader identifies a partial-success state instead of one generic authentication failure.

argumentNodes.question: How can exception structure erase evidence?
argumentNodes.claim: Putting remote exchange and local persistence under one catch sends semantically different failures into the same fallback and can trigger misleading reauthorization.
argumentNodes.readerProgress: The reader sees catch boundaries as part of the reliability model.

argumentNodes.question: What does fail-visible propagation improve?
argumentNodes.claim: Propagating the storage fault preserves which side committed so retry, reconciliation or operator handling can start from the actual state.
argumentNodes.readerProgress: The reader understands why visibility is a prerequisite for recovery but not recovery itself.

argumentNodes.question: What remains unsolved?
argumentNodes.claim: The change supplies no rollback, distributed atomicity, exactly-once storage or universal retry policy; provider and server semantics remain decisive.
argumentNodes.readerProgress: The reader avoids treating better error propagation as transactional correctness.

counterpoint.claim: Some clients prefer automatic reauthorization because local token storage is disposable and forward progress matters more than preserving partial state.
counterpoint.responseBoundary: That policy can be valid only when explicitly declared; it should not arise accidentally from a catch that cannot distinguish exchange failure from persistence failure.

endingStrategy.purpose: End with structured partial-success errors, provider durability contracts and headless operator alerts.
